claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC microstructure.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 30% strain.
The proposed intervention adds approximately 5 at% Mo to TiVNbTa.
The modified alloy is to be sintered and then aged near 1000 K for several hours in an inert atmosphere.
Mo addition and aging will produce nanometer-scale, uniformly distributed Mo-rich precipitates in the BCC matrix.
Fine precipitates can produce precipitation strengthening in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed Mo-rich precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
Mo-rich precipitates will stabilize the high-temperature BCC phase.
The intervention will delay grain coarsening at elevated temperature.
The intervention will increase the TiVNbTa yield strength at 1273 K from approximately 330 MPa to more than 400 MPa.
The modified alloy will maintain or slightly enhance ductility.
The modified alloy will retain unchanged thermal conductivity.
The modified alloy will transfer heat efficiently between W and CuCrZr.
The enhanced performance is expected near 1273 K under loading up to approximately 30% strain.
This temperature and loading range is compatible with the thermal limits of the adjoining W and CuCrZr components.
Poor homogenization or aging optimization could produce microstructural heterogeneity or unwanted secondary phases and diminish strengthening.
Observation of nonuniform or deleterious precipitates would falsify the proposed precipitation-strengthening mechanism.

contradictions.description: The uncertainty field treats nonuniform precipitates as a failure to optimize processing and realize the intended mediator, whereas the falsification rule treats the same observation as falsifying the precipitation-strengthening mechanism itself. Failure to form the proposed precipitates does not by itself test whether such precipitates would strengthen the alloy.
